headlines.summary: The 737 Max 10, the largest model in the family, was set to start flying in 2020, but increased scrutiny and other safety issues delayed its certification.
headlines.article_text: Boeing wins FAA approval for 737 Max 10 after years of delays Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points The FAA certified Boeing's 737 Max 10, the largest model in the best-selling family of aircraft. The plane, which was set to start flying in 2020, is years behind schedule after safety crises and engineering changes. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told CNBC that the U.S. needs to speed up its certification process In this article BA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:22 01:22 FAA certifies Boeing 737 Max-10 Closing Bell The Federal Aviation Administration on Tuesday signed off on the Boeing 737 Max 10 after years of delays , a major win for the manufacturer and the last in Boeing's best-selling family of jets to get government approval. The green light comes weeks after federal officials reviewed a navigation system glitch on the aircraft but deemed it was not a safety-of-flight issue. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told CNBC's Phil LeBeau that safety is paramount, but he also said the U.S. needs to improve its certification process. "It takes Boeing, to certify an aircraft in Europe, about half the time, less than half the time that it does in the U.S. You have China now playing to take over in aviation," Duffy said. "We have to certify aircraft more quickly if we're going to compete as Americans." The 737 Max 10, the largest model in the family that can seat up to 230 people, was set to start flying in 2020, but increased scrutiny following two Max crashes in 2018 and 2019 and other safety issues delayed its certification. Engineering changes were also required, including to an anti-icing system for the aircraft's engines. Max 10 customers include Alaska Airlines , American Airlines , United Airlines and Delta Air Lines . Boeing said the Max 10 makes up about 30% of its Max backlog. Airlines can finally start flying passengers soon after planes are certified, but it can take months for carriers to work them into schedules. United CEO Scott Kirby told CNBC in August that the airline had been waiting so long for the Max 10 that the lie-flat seats it expected for the plane no longer make sense and are sitting in a warehouse. Alaska Airlines last month said it plans to put lie-flat seats on some of its 737 Max 10s in a push for more premium offerings. The FAA approved the smallest model of the 737 Max family, the Max 7 , in early August. Boeing has been working to ramp up production of its 737 Maxes and 787 Dreamliners, which are key to its recovery since airlines and other customers pay the bulk of the aircraft's price upon delivery. The manufacturer opened a fourth production line in Everett, Washington, in July for its 737 Max airplanes. headlines.article_text: SpaceX (SPCX) Q3 2026 earnings report: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 2:20 02:20 SpaceX earnings in focus as Starlink growth and AI spending take center stage Morning Call SpaceX reported 161% revenue growth for the third quarter, beating Wall Street estimates, as the company's artificial intelligence business grew ninefold. The stock rose about 3% in extended trading on Tuesday. Here's how the company did compared to LSEG consensus estimates: Revenue: $14.58 billion vs. $12.72 billion expected Earnings per share: 35 cents It's not immediately clear if the reported earnings are comparable to the LSEG analyst estimate. SpaceX said in a release that it recorded operating income of $2.8 billion and net income of $4.4 billion. In the same period a year earlier, SpaceX reported a net loss of $1.05 billion. While SpaceX is best known for its reusable rockets, most of its revenue and profit in recent quarters came from the company's connectivity segment, which consists of its Starlink satellite internet service. Starlink's subscribers base grew to 13.6 million in the quarter, up from 12 million in the prior period. Total connectivity revenue jumped 69% to $5.25 billion from $3.1 billion a year earlier. Analysts were expecting $4.84 billion, according to StreetAccount. Revenue from consumer Starlink subscribers amounted to $3.12 billion, while the company generated $2.13 billion from government and enterprise customers. Buzz has been building about Starlink's plans to build a U.S. mobile network after SpaceX, earlier this month, announced that it's buying 800 MHz of low-band spectrum, and after the Federal Communications Commission approved a plan for the company to build out a 15,000-satellite constellation. SpaceX jumped into AI with the purchase earlier this year of xAI, which was Elon Musk's AI lab. The company has been rapidly expanding that business by renting out capacity to Google , Anthropic and others. AI, which the company now calls "Super Intelligence," has emerged as SpaceX's largest business. Revenue jumped ninefold to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the same quarter last year. Analysts expected sales of $6.47 billion, according to StreetAccount. During the third quarter, SpaceX also closed its $60 billion purchase of AI coding startup Cursor. Meanwhile, SpaceX's launch business was up just slightly in the quarter, with sales rising to $1.77 billion from $1.67 billion a year ago. Almost all of SpaceX's profit still comes from Starlink. Operating income in the connectivity unit about doubled to $2.37 billion. The AI business swung to a profit of $431 million, while the space division lost $7 million. Of its $19.6 billion in capital expenditures in the quarter, more than $16.4 billion was committed to the AI business. Musk said on the company's call that SpaceX aims to "deploy power, cooling infrastructure at a rate that is vastly faster than anyone else." In its Memphis-area data centers, SpaceX's AI business is on track to be able to bring 200,000 of Nvidia's Grace Blackwell system online "every month for the remainder of this year." —Lora Kolodny 15 Min Ago Starlink subscriber count rises to 13.6 million SpaceX reported that its Starlink subscriber count rose to 13.6 million in Q3, with average revenue per user increasing to $69, up from the June quarter when the company reported 12 million Starlink subscribers and ARPU of $66. About $3.12 billion of SpaceX's $5.25 billion in total Connectivity revenue came from consumer subscribers, while government and enterprise customers generated $2.13 billion in the segment. The company boasted in an investor update that Starlink was activated in over 3,800 aircraft as of the quarter's end. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk recently threatened Delta CEO Ed Bastian saying he would lose his job because his airline has not yet made Starlink wireless internet available in their planes. 2 Hours Ago SpaceX earnings call coming half hour after the close SpaceX is scheduled to hold its third-quarter earnings call at 4:30 p.m. ET. Analysts expect revenue at the electric vehicle maker to dip slightly from a year ago to $27.9 billion, according to LSEG. Tesla shares are down about 17% this year as of Tuesday, leaving the company with a market cap of almost $1.5 billion. —Ari Levy 3 Hours Ago Tough time for neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius in October SpaceX is relatively new to the cloud computing business. Many of its competitors in the space, the so-called neoclouds, have been getting hammered on Wall Street of late on concerns that rising interest rates are going to make the costly buildout financially burdensome. CoreWeave and Nebius are down 28% so far in October, while IREN has plunged about 35%. Earlier this month, Australian AI data center operator Firmus withdrew its planned IPO, citing market volatility and conditions. While SpaceX is far less reliant on that side of its business than are the neoclouds, capital costs still matter, and the company is banking on the AI boom continuing. In the second quarter, debt and finance leases increased to $36.8 billion, up from $22 billion the prior period. —Ari Levy 4 Hours Ago How the stock has done since the IPO Billboards in Times Square celebrate the SpaceX IPO debut at the Nasdaq on June 12th, 2026. The stock hit a low of $104.83 on Aug. 3, a few days before the first post-IPO lockup expired, making more than 911 million SpaceX shares available for trading. The lockup lifted on Aug. 6, and the stock rallied, popping 6% initially, then nearly 16% the day after. —Lora Kolodny 5 Hours Ago Starship hits several milestones, but is still being tested The SpaceX Starship and Super Heavy v3 Booster lift off on its 14th test flight from the SpaceX launch complex in Starbase, Texas, US, September 28, 2026. headlines.summary: Wall Street and investors will be looking for Netflix to provide additional details about the company's strategy following recent organizational changes
headlines.article_text: Netflix (NFLX) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Netflix reported third-quarter earnings per share that surpassed Wall Street expectations and revenue that was in line. The streaming giant in its shareholder letter said, "We know there's some investor concern about our view hours growth," but added, "engagement — which encompasses quantity, quality and variety of viewing — remains healthy." Wall Street and investors will be looking for Netflix to provide additional details about the company's strategy following recent organizational changes. In this article NFLX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:33 01:33 Netflix shares fall more than 6% on lower Q4 revenue outlook Closing Bell: Overtime Netflix on Tuesday reported third-quarter earnings that topped analyst estimates and revenue that was in line as Wall Street eyes the company's engagement and advertising metrics. Here's how Netflix performed for the period ended Sept. 30, compared with projections from analysts polled by LSEG: Earnings per share: 87 cents vs. 82 cents estimated Revenue: $12.87 billion vs. $12.87 billion estimated The streamer's revenue was almost 12% higher year over year, boosted by growth in membership and an increase in subscription prices that went into effect in March, the company said. Netflix said the response to those price hikes has been consistent with prior changes and with its expectations. Net income for the quarter was $3.66 billion, or 87 cents per share, compared with $2.55 billion, or 59 cents a share in the same period last year. Netflix said the year-over-year jump in profit was due in part to the timing of expenses. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue to rise more than 11% to $13.44 billion, driven by growth in memberships, pricing and ad revenue, it said. The company narrowed its 2026 full-year forecast, saying it now expects revenue to reach $51.1 billion, a 13% increase over the year prior. This is on the low end of the range Netflix provided during its previous earnings report of between $51 billion and $51.4 billion and below Wall Street's expectations of $51.2 billion for the year, according to LSEG. Shares of Netflix fell about 4% in extended trading Tuesday. Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty Images Wall Street and investors will be looking for Netflix to provide additional details about the company's strategy following recent organizational changes and headwinds including stagnating viewership and growing competition from the likes of YouTube. "With intense competition and an explosion of content competing for consumer attention, strategic clarity and excellent execution are critical," the company said in a shareholder letter Tuesday. "In Q3, we delivered well across all three priorities, but we see room to do even better with focused, continuous improvement." Last week, Netflix said it was laying off about 6% of employees, or roughly 1,000 workers, and that Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria was departing from that role. The company said Tuesday it expects its fourth-quarter results to be impacted by those headcount reductions, with a negative impact on operating margin of about 120 basis points. Former Disney executive Peter Rice has been tapped as the new CCO, but it's not yet clear how he'll address concerns around viewership. Netflix in its shareholder letter said, "We know there's some investor concern about our view hours growth," but added, "engagement — which encompasses quantity, quality and variety of viewing — remains healthy and … we continue to deliver strong value to members." The company seeks to accelerate growth in those view hours and plans to do so with a three-step strategy, it said: deliver more entertainment value to members; leverage technology to improve all aspects of the service; and improve monetization. Central to Netflix's value offering has been its cheaper, ad-supported tier. Yet, the company on Tuesday lowered its full-year revenue guidance for its ad business. Netflix said it now expects 2026 ad revenue of around $2.7 billion, down from the roughly $3 billion the company had previously forecast. That lower guidance is due to a slower-than-expected rollout of some ad product capabilities, the company said. Earlier Tuesday, Netflix announced new features for advertisers that it says will help better connect brands to the right audiences and measure the impact of their ads. In this article CRM BRZE Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Sheldon Cooper | Lightrocket | Getty Images Salesforce announced an agreement Tuesday to buy customer engagement platform Braze in a deal worth about $5.66 billion. The transaction is expected to close in fiscal 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, according to a Salesforce blog . The stock skyrocketed more than 51% on Tuesday to close at $45.57 after a brief halt premarket following the news. "Salesforce's platform will help us innovate faster and together we'll help marketers around the world build deeper, more lasting relationships with their customers." The latest deal comes just months after Salesforce announced it would buy AI customer service platform Fin for about $3.6 billion, in a move meant to bolster the company's agentic AI offerings for enterprises. headlines.summary: GM narrowed its 2026 earnings guidance and raised its adjusted automotive free cash flow outlook after beating Wall Street’s third-quarter estimates.
headlines.article_text: General Motors (GM) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points General Motors beat Wall Street’s expectations on the top- and bottom-lines. The Detroit automaker raised its free cash flow expectations and narrowed its 2026 full-year guidance. GM also announced a new multiyear stock buyback of $20 billion, but didn’t give a specific timeframe for the repurchase. In this article GM Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 7:11 07:11 GM CFO Paul Jacobson on $20B stock buyback: Driven by our stellar free cash flow generation Squawk Box DETROIT — General Motors narrowed its 2026 earnings guidance and raised its free cash flow expectations after beating Wall Street's third-quarter expectations. The Detroit automaker also announced a new multiyear stock buyback of $20 billion after GM completed a $6 billion share repurchase program that was announced in January. GM did not disclose a specific time to complete the program. Despite the positive news, GM stock fell nearly 7% during trading Tuesday as the company's outlook missed Wall Street's expectations. Wall Street analysts were mixed before the report on whether GM would raise its guidance Tuesday amid concerns of slowing sales and rising commodity costs. Analysts' expectations included a midpoint of $13.41 per share for the year compared with GM's new $13.25 per share midpoint, according to LSEG. Several analysts in investor notes Tuesday said GM's third-quarter results were solid, but raised concerns about whether higher costs and pressures on vehicle pricing would limit earnings growth next year. Here's how GM performed in the third quarter, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG: Earnings per share: $3.70 adjusted vs. $3.63 expected Revenue: $50.02 billion vs. $48.7 billion expected GM's new guidance includes adjusted earnings before interest and taxes of between $14.5 billion and $15.5 billion, or $12.75 to $13.75 adjusted earnings per share, and adjusted automotive free cash flow of between $11.5 billion and $12.5 billion. That compares with its raised guidance from July that included adjusted EBIT of between $14 billion and $16 billion, or $12 to $14 adjusted EPS, and adjusted automotive free cash flow of $9.5 billion to $11.5 billion. "I think the market's been pretty consistent from what we've said all year," GM CFO Paul Jacobson told CNBC's Phil LeBeau . "Our fourth quarter's going to be down sequentially. ... I think the fact that we're able to hold our guidance in the face of that late inflationary pressure in the year is another sign of the GM team executing really well." Mary Barra, chair and chief executive officer of General Motors Co., during a news conference at the Hudson's building in Detroit, Michigan, US, on Monday, April 15, 2024. Jeff Kowalsky | Bloomberg | Getty Images GM on Tuesday said it expects commodity inflation costs to be around $2 billion, which was the high end of its previous guidance. That includes higher costs for logistics and dynamic random-access memory, or DRAM, chips that are impacting multiple industries . While the inflationary costs were at the automaker's high end of guidance, GM said its gross tariff costs are expected to be at the low end of its expected $2.5 billion to $3.5 billion range. Warranty costs are expected to be at high end between $1 billion and $1.5 billion, GM said. Jacobson said vehicle pricing is relatively flat as inflationary costs continue to increase. He said the company would assess where consumers are in the coming year when deciding if it should pass costs along by raising prices more than normal. "GM is performing well, and we are working hard to continue our momentum despite growing inflationary pressures through strategic investments in new products and services, and through improved quality and operating efficiency," GM CEO Mary Barra said Tuesday in a letter to shareholders. The automaker also said the costs of its pullback in all-electric vehicles announced last year were "substantially completed," saying it has recorded $11.2 billion in such charges since the second half of last year, including paying $4.6 billion of $7.4 billion in cash through the third quarter. The company's net income attributed to stockholders was $3.3 billion during the third quarter, up roughly $2 billion from a year earlier. GM's North American operations continued to lead the automaker's results, accounting for $3.6 billion of its $4.1 billion in adjusted EBIT results during the third quarter. GM's 2025 third-quarter results included $48.59 billion in revenue, net income attributable to stockholders of $1.3 billion and earnings per share of $2.80 adjusted.
